statement: A top-5 developer reports AI systems did >= 50% of code or experiments in a frontier training project (technical report or system card; by 2028-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Not met. AI code generation was assistive: a Bloc A developer measured its internal ML completion completing >3% of code; a code assistant vendor reported ~40% of code in files where it is enabled (general developers, not frontier training projects). In the window, a top-5 developer's competitive-programming system was published in a peer-reviewed journal at roughly median-competitor level. No report of AI doing a share of frontier training work.

items.summary: A top-5 developer's competitive-programming system, published in a peer-reviewed journal, placed around the median competitor (top ~54%) in 10 recent online contests - the first AI code-generation system at competitive level. Not used for its own research workflows.
items.detail: DeepMind, 'Competitive programming with AlphaCode' (first published 2022-02-02, updated after Science publication on 2022-12-08; verified via web_extract this run). The Science article itself was blocked (403).

items.summary: A top-5 developer reported that its internal transformer-based hybrid code completion, used by 10k+ internal developers, completes about 3% of code with a 25-34% acceptance rate and a 6% reduction in coding iteration time.
items.detail: Google Research blog, 'ML-Enhanced Code Completion Improves Developer Productivity', 2022-07-26 (updated 2022-09-06; verified via web_extract this run).

items.summary: A code-assistant vendor (affiliated with a top-5 developer's partner) reported that in files where its assistant is enabled, nearly 40% of code is written by it in popular languages; general developer population, not a frontier training project.
items.detail: GitHub blog, 'GitHub Copilot is generally available to all developers', 2022-06-21 (verified via web_extract this run): 1.2M technical-preview users; 'nearly 40% of code is being written by GitHub Copilot' in enabled files (e.g. Python). Vendor self-report.
